title: Profit target display follow-ups (batch PR #207) — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #207 (batched: frontend-trend-strength-chart-followups, frontend-volume-indicators-chart-followups, frontend-divergence-markers-followups, frontend-tide-region-chart-shading-followups, frontend-profit-target-display-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. Both findings below isolate specifically to frontend-profit-target-display-followups' own changes (RewardRiskBadge.tsx and the new frontend/src/utils/profitTargetHelpText.ts) -- the PR's other four batched changes had no findings of any kind (see PR #207's review comment for the full verification detail across all five).

checklist.step: RewardRiskBadge.tsx's new `failureAriaLabel` prop (this PR) parameterizes the *content* of the warning icon's `aria-label`, but doesn't fix the pre-existing (not introduced by this PR) reason that label is never actually announced to a screen reader at all: MUI's `SvgIcon` (which `WarningAmberIcon` wraps) defaults `aria-hidden="true"` whenever no `titleAccess` prop is supplied, and neither the old nor the new code passes one -- confirmed live (PR #207 browser walkthrough, MU stock detail page): the rendered DOM has both `aria-hidden="true"` and `aria-label="Below the 2:1 minimum"` on the same `<svg>` simultaneously, and `aria-hidden="true"` removes an element from the accessibility tree regardless of any `aria-label` also present. Testing-library's `getByLabelText` (used by both the pre-existing and this PR's new RewardRiskBadge.test.tsx assertions) matches on the raw `aria-label` attribute directly, not a real accessibility-tree computation, so the existing unit tests pass despite this. Fix by either passing MUI's `titleAccess` prop (which also clears the default `aria-hidden`) instead of a bare `aria-label`, or explicitly overriding `aria-hidden={false}` alongside the existing `aria-label` prop.

The new frontend/src/utils/profitTargetHelpText.ts (PROFIT_TARGET_DEFINITION / PROFIT_TARGET_ELDER_CONTEXT_SUFFIX) is domain-specific content (Elder ch. 58's Tradebill 'A' target formula, Autoenvelope/channel height, protective stop, ch. 53's 2:1 rule) shared across exactly two features (features/stocks and features/portfolio), placed in `utils/` specifically to avoid a cross-feature registry import. This is a genuinely arguable case (not a clear-cut misplacement) given the task's own explicit, well-reasoned decisions entry, but it does read as in tension with Frontend.md §3's own placement test ('references a feature's domain concept... -> features/<domain>/'; `utils/` is documented as for helpers that are 'domain-agnostic', which this text isn't) -- `utils/insiderClusters.ts` is a prior, narrower precedent (a single-feature helper, not genuinely cross-feature content) that doesn't fully cover this case either. Worth either (a) documenting this specific pattern (domain-specific content genuinely shared by exactly two feature registries, where neither owns it and cross-importing one from the other is the established anti-pattern) as an explicit, named exception in Frontend.md §3 alongside the existing utils/ placement rule, or (b) reconsidering whether a small third location (e.g. a features/shared/ or similar) would fit this and any future same-shaped case better than `utils/`.
